title: Saag Paneer Lasagne
changes_from_base: A spiced spinach saag with chilli, coriander and fenugreek and coarsely grated paneer replace the meat ragù, layered with a nutmeg and parmesan béchamel.
summary: A spiced twist on lasagne layering a fragrant blended spinach saag with grated paneer and a nutmeg-scented béchamel.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm baking dish at least 5 cm deep

ingredients.item: green chillies (such as serrano), stalks removed, halved lengthwise
bunch fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Wilt
steps.text: Boil a large pot of water, add the 455 g spinach and once fully wilted after about 2 min drain in the colander and cool under cold water, keeping the pot.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Put the drained spinach in the blender with the 2 tomatoes, 2 chillies, coriander, 3 tbsp fenugreek if using and 180 ml water, blend 30-60 seconds until smooth and season with salt.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: In the same pot melt the 40 g ghee over medium, cook the 150 g onion 6-8 min until golden, then add the garlic and 1½ tbsp ginger and stir 2 min.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Stir in the Kashmiri chilli, 1½ tbsp ground coriander, 2 tsp cumin and 1 tsp turmeric with a little salt, add the saag and simmer gently 10-12 min until slightly thicker.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Melt the 115 g butter over low heat, whisk in the 65 g flour for 2-3 min until golden, add the 950 ml milk and stir 5-8 min until it coats a spoon, then off the heat whisk in pepper, nutmeg and 40 g parmesan and season.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C and grease the dish, spread a thin layer of sauce over the base, then layer sheets, a third of the saag, a third of the 370 g paneer and a quarter of the remaining sauce, repeating twice.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Top with a last layer of sheets, the rest of the sauce and the remaining parmesan.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover with lightly greased foil and bake 40 min, then uncover and bake about 20 min until the sheets are tender and the top is light golden.

tips: Blend the spinach only briefly to keep the saag a vivid green.
Turn the heat down if the onions or garlic start to catch so they stay sweet.
Loosen the béchamel with a little milk if it thickens too much before layering.
storage: The saag and sauce can each be made 2 days ahead and chilled, and leftovers freeze for up to 3 months, thawed overnight in the fridge before reheating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
